Process

How I work on every site

The same four steps on every site. The output of step four becomes the input of step one, so each cycle starts with better data than the last.

STEP 01

Research

Read the SERP and tear down the pages that rank: structure, intent, entities, SERP features and positioning.

STEP 02

Map

Assign every intent to one URL. Decide what the product page should own and what a guide should own.

STEP 03

Ship

Make the changes in the CMS: copy, metadata, headings, internal links, schema and technical fixes.

STEP 04

Measure

Log each change with a date, compare before and after in GSC and GA4, and feed the result into the next round.

Every change is logged and measured, so you can see which work moved the numbers and repeat it.

Who I work with

SaaS product teams and agencies

SaaS and product companies

Your website, free tool and paid product often compete for the same searches. I make sure each search lands on the right page.

  • Template systems for use-case, comparison and alternative pages that scale without thin content.

Agencies and client teams

  • Multi-site execution: 25+ client sites and a 40+ site local portfolio at the same time.
  • Local SEO and Google Business Profiles: categories, services, posts, citations and local schema.
  • SOPs and briefs that let writers and specialists deliver to one standard.
  • Client-ready reporting that explains results in plain language.

My background

I trained as a mechatronics and control engineer at UET Lahore. Control systems teach one habit above all: change one input, measure the output, adjust. That's how I do SEO.

I started as a technical writer, explaining cybersecurity, compliance, automotive and SaaS products to people who need to understand them before they buy. That taught me to write pages that rank and still make sense to a buyer.

As SEO Content Writing Lead at Proteus Technologies, I led a team of three SEO writers across B2B SaaS and martech clients, including Certrec's compliance platform. I wrote white papers, datasheets and landing pages, and built content funnels that bring in organic traffic and capture it as leads.

Today, as On-page SEO Strategist at Repstack, an Inc. 5000 company, I run SEO across 25+ client websites for AI, automation and SaaS clients, a 40+ site local lead-generation portfolio, and an SEO software product. On the side, I lecture and assess Digital Marketing at GBS Dubai, which keeps me sharp on both the practical and strategic sides of the field.

CASE 02

SEO software product: competitive research and keyword architecture

SaaSCompetitor teardownKeyword mapping
Client
A SaaS product in the SEO software space (Repstack client)
My role
SEO specialist: planning and execution
Focus
Competitive product analysis, keyword-to-page mapping, landing pages

The challenge

SEO tools are one of the most crowded software categories in search. Established brands own the head terms, and every competitor publishes the same comparison and how-to content. A newer product has to find the intents nobody serves well and win those first.

What I did

  • Ran a competitive product analysis from public sources: competitor websites, landing pages, page structures, keyword coverage and positioning.
  • Mapped commercial and informational keywords to product, feature and content pages, separating what the product page should own from what a guide should own.
  • Turned the findings into a prioritized plan for page structure, metadata, internal linking and new content, then optimized the landing pages against it.

The teardown framework I use

LAYER 1Page architectureWhich intents each competitor gives its own URL, and how those pages link
LAYER 2On-pageTitles, H1s, headings, entity coverage, FAQs, calls to action
LAYER 3SERP featuresSnippets, People Also Ask, AI Overviews, video and reviews
LAYER 4PositioningClaims, proof, free-tier hooks and pricing messages on public pages
LAYER 5GapsIntents nobody serves well: the fastest place for a challenger to rank

Each intent gets its own page, and the free tool sits on the page that wins the search. Built from patterns that are visible in public search results.
